newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian army units clash north of capital.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian army units clash north of capital.

text.p: Fighting erupted between Cambodian government army units near Phnom Penh but was not connected to the feud between the country's two prime ministers, military officials said on Wednesday.
The fighting, at Preak Kadam, 30 km (20 miles) north of the capital, was sparked by a local dispute, General Mol Reup, a military adviser to Second Prime Minster Hun Sen, told Reuters.
"The fighting was not between FUNCINPEC and CPP," he said, referring to the royalist FUNCINPEC party of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranridhh and to Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
Mol Reup said the clash erupted late on Tuesday and continued into Wednesday over a group of soldiers extorting money from passing vehicles.
One senior army officer was shot in the clash but his condition was not known, he said. He said he was not aware of any other casualties.
A witness in the area said there had been several incidents involving troops at checkpoints prior to Tuesday night's clash.
Government troops and military police had been sent to the area and calm had been restored, government officials said.
The clash came as political tension ran high in Phnom Penh, with consistent reports of troop movements in and around the capital.
Hun Sen warned earlier this week he would use force if he found Ranariddh's military men bringing troops into Phnom Penh illegally. Ranariddh denied he was moving troops into the city.
Security units loyal to the two prime ministers fought a gun battle in central Phnom Penh on June 17. Two of Ranariddh's bodyguards died in the battle.
There has been mounting international concern about political stability and violence in Cambodia in recent weeks with the government crippled by the ongoing feud between the prime ministers.

Hun Sen and Ranariddh head a fractured coalition formed after a U.N.-supervised election in 1993. Relations between the two deteriorated sharply last year when Ranariddh demanded a greater share of power to govern in the provinces.
